/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 21 October 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2680 (87)
Baltic Capesize Index: 3793 (271)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2204 (-43)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1870 (2)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1019 (2)
CAPESIZE
The market continued to build momentum, with gains across both basins lifting the BCI 182 5TC by $2,453 to $34,398. The C5 index advanced by $1.160 to $14.160, while C3 gained $1.275 to reach $33.175. In the Pacific, healthy demand and talk of potential weather-related delays in China helped support sentiment. Operators set the tone early on C5, opening bids at $13.00 against offers in excess of $14.00. One miner was heard bidding $13.60 against an offer of $14.10, although no fixture had been confirmed at the time of writing, while the second miner remained out of the market. An operator was meanwhile reported to have paid $14.10, providing further support to rising rate expectations. The Atlantic also gained traction, with brokers describing well-supported conditions from both South Brazil and West Africa to China amid healthy demand. Offers for early index dates were reported in the mid-$32s, while later dates continued to command a premium with bids pushing past $33. With positive sentiment spreading across both basins and weather concerns potentially adding further support, the market closed on a firmer footing, with owners looking for further gains.
PANAMAX
The market remained under pressure today, with sentiment across the Atlantic continuing to soften as charterers were said to maintain the upper hand. While a reasonable volume of fixing activity was seen earlier in the week, a lack of cargo replenishment has resulted in available tonnage continuing to outpace demand. Trans-Atlantic business was reported to be losing further momentum, with limited fresh enquiry and little urgency from charterers to cover requirements. Recent mineral fixtures were concluded below previously achieved levels, while grain demand remained subdued. Fronthaul activity also disappointed, with owners described as increasingly willing to accept lower levels in order to try and secure employment. Conditions in EC South America remained particularly difficult, with market sources describing a persistent excess of tonnage and insufficient cargo demand to absorb supply. In contrast, the Pacific proved more resilient, with rates broadly holding steady despite a relatively subdued trading environment. Market participants noted that EC Australian demand continued to generate interest, particularly for later loading dates, providing some support to regional values. The GNS Honour (81,398 2011) open Hong Kong 19 October was reported to have fixed a trip via EC Australia to Singapore-Japan range with coal at around $22,250. The P5TC declined by $387 on the day to $19,836.
SUPRAMAX
Another rather subdued day, despite being the halfway point of the week, with the 11TC average up $23 to close at $23,638. Early US Gulf vessels came under pressure as most of the demand has now shifted to November dates, with fronthaul offers particularly hard hit and sources saying there was a lack of petcoke stems now, although north coast South America has bucked the trend. The South Atlantic is holding up better in comparison, with levels remaining mainly flat, as enough fresh demand emerged to support the tonnage list. The Mediterranean is positional with vessels again having to consider ballasting as an alternative, whilst the Continent is much quieter than the last few weeks. In Asia there has been fewer reported NoPac trades despite the grains season continuing, but backhauls have taken up the slack with Operators keen to take short period against the right first leg. South East Asia was still active, with rates to India improving, helped by increased Australian stems which are drawing vessels from East coast India and Chittagong. There has been little reported from South Africa, however sources felt rates remained close to last done levels.
HANDYSIZE
A generally quiet day was reported across both basins, with little fresh information emerging. The BHSI rose by 2 points to 1,019, while the 7TC average increased by $31 to settle at $18,336. In the Continent and Mediterranean, the market remained broadly flat, with rates holding around previous levels. The South Atlantic maintained positive sentiment, supported by a healthy volume of enquiry and an increasingly tight tonnage list. In contrast, the US Gulf saw little activity, with limited demand and an oversupply of tonnage continuing to weigh on rates. Meanwhile, the Asian market maintained its momentum, with rates discussed around last-done levels and prompt owners showing some resistance.

Atlantic
A 39,000-dwt was fixed from the US Gulf to the NC South America with grains at $17,500, although further details were not disclosed.

Asia
The Centurion Lucilla (40,054 2021) open Zhoushan ex-drydock on 20 October was fixed by XO for a trip to Chittagong with steels with redelivery Penang in the $18,000s, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Chinese Iron Ore Imports by Origin

In 3Q26, Chinese iron ore imports edged 0.8 Mt higher on the year to 109.8 Mt, following increased shipments from Brazil (+2.2 Mt to 79.1 Mt), India (+1.6 Mt to 5.1 Mt) and Guinea (+5.8 Mt to 6.0 Mt), though imports fell from Australia (-6.2 Mt to 189.7 Mt), Canada (-3.2 Mt to 2.6 Mt) and South Africa (-0.8 Mt to 10.7 Mt), customs data show.

Chinese Bauxite Imports

In September, Chinese bauxite imports rose 2.5 Mt year-on-year to 18.3 Mt, although 3q26 inbound shipments stood 1.2 Mt below last year at 52.8 Mt, customs data show. Third quarter shipments from Guinea climbed 1.7 Mt to 40.2 Mt, countered by a decline in shipments from Malaysia (-0.5 Mt to 0.1 Mt) and Brazil (-0.4 Mt to none).

[Sent from Front]

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape saw a strong rally throughout the session, with significant activity across Nov, Dec and the cal as prices pushed higher. Oct strengthened from 33,100 to 33,750, while Nov opened at 35,250 before rallying to 37,650, with heavy volume around 37,000–37,500. Dec improved from 36,250 to 37,850, with strong afternoon activity. Q4 26 strengthened from 34,500 to 36,100, while Q1 27 rose from 29,000 to 29,500, with good late volume.
